questions.question: Which of the following two countries hosted the Second G20 Anti-Corruption Working Group in June 2025?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Brazil and South Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second G20 Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG)** meeting in **June 2025** was a significant event hosted under the collaborative efforts of **Brazil** and **South Africa**.
 
• **South Africa** officially assumed the **G20 Presidency** on **December 1, 2024**, taking over from **Brazil**. The **2025** calendar of meetings, including those in **June**, reflects the transition and thematic continuity between the two nations.
 
• The **Anti-Corruption Working Group** (ACWG) is tasked with leading the **G20’s** efforts to fight corruption by implementing the **G20 Anti-Corruption Action Plan**.
 
• The hosting by **Brazil** and **South Africa** emphasizes the "Global South" leadership within the **G20**, focusing on issues such as **asset recovery** and **transparency in the public sector**.
 
• The **June 2025** meeting aimed to strengthen legal frameworks for **extradition** and **mutual legal assistance** among member countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The G20 Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG):**
 
 
• The **ACWG** was established at the **Toronto Summit** in **2010**. Its primary objective is to develop and implement a comprehensive anti-corruption agenda across **G20** member states.
 
• It works closely with international organizations such as the **United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)**, the **OECD**, and the **World Bank** to ensure global compliance with anti-corruption standards.
 
 
 
• **The G20 Presidency Transition:**
 
 
• The **G20** operates on a system of rotating presidencies. **Brazil** held the presidency in **2024**, followed by **South Africa** in **2025**.
 
• **South Africa’s** presidency in **2025** is historic, marking the first time a **G20 Summit** and its ministerial meetings are hosted on the **African continent**.
 
 
 
• **Core Themes of ACWG 2025:**
 
 
• Key focus areas include **beneficial ownership transparency**, which aims to reveal the true owners of corporate entities to prevent **money laundering**.
 
• The group also prioritizes **protecting whistleblowers** and enhancing integrity in the **private sector** to foster a fair global economic environment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The G20 Troika:**
 
 
• The **Troika** for **2025** consists of the previous host (**Brazil**), the current host (**South Africa**), and the upcoming host for **2026** (the **United States**). This structure ensures consistency in the **G20** agenda.
 
 
 
• **Global Significance:**
 
 
• The **G20** members represent around **85%** of the global **GDP**, over **75%** of global trade, and about **two-thirds** of the world population.
 
• In **2023**, the **African Union** became a permanent member of the **G20** under the **Indian Presidency**, further increasing the representation of developing nations during the **2024 (Brazil)** and **2025 (South Africa)** tenures.

questions.question: The Indian Navy’s home-built Shivalik-class stealth frigate equipped with guided missiles that took part in the JAIMEX-25 naval exercise held from 16 to 18 October 2025 was ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**INS Sahyadri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Navy's** home-built **Shivalik-class** stealth frigate, **INS Sahyadri**, represented India in the **JAIMEX-25** naval exercise.
 
• The exercise was conducted over three days, from **16 to 18 October 2025**, focusing on high-end maritime operations and interoperability.
 
• **INS Sahyadri** is a multi-role **stealth frigate** equipped with advanced **guided missiles**, making it a potent platform for anti-air, anti-surface, and anti-submarine warfare.
 
• The **JAIMEX** (Japan-India Maritime Exercise) series highlights the growing strategic partnership and maritime cooperation between the **Indian Navy** and the **Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF)**.
 
• This participation underscores India's "**Atmanirbhar Bharat**" (Self-reliant India) initiative, as the ship is a product of indigenous design and construction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shivalik-class Frigates (Project 17):**
 
 
• These are the first **stealth warships** built in India. The class includes three ships: **INS Shivalik**, **INS Satpura**, and **INS Sahyadri**.
 
• They were designed by the **Indian Navy's Directorate of Naval Design** and constructed at **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL)** in **Mumbai**.
 
• The **stealth features** include a reduced **Radar Cross Section (RCS)** and specialized hull forms to minimize noise and infrared signatures.
 
 
 
• **INS Sahyadri (F45):**
 
 
• Commissioned on **21 July 2012**, it is the third ship of the **Shivalik class**.
 
• The ship is named after the **Sahyadri mountain range** (Western Ghats) in India.
 
• It has a displacement of approximately **6,200 tonnes** and can reach speeds exceeding **30 knots**.
 
 
 
• **Weaponry and Sensors:**
 
 
• The vessel is armed with **BrahMos** or **Klub** anti-ship cruise missiles and **Barak-1** or **Shtil-1** air defense missile systems.
 
• It also features **RBU-6000** anti-submarine rocket launchers and **DTA-53** torpedo launchers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** Exercises like **JAIMEX-25** are crucial for ensuring a **Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP)**, a shared vision between **India** and **Japan**.
 
• **Interoperability:** The exercise involved complex maneuvers, including **cross-deck helicopter operations**, tactical exercises, and communication drills to enhance the synergy between the two navies.
 
• **Evolution of Stealth:** The success of the **Shivalik-class** paved the way for the more advanced **Project 17A (Nilgiri-class)** frigates, which feature even more significant stealth characteristics and updated technology.
 
• **Global Reach:** **INS Sahyadri** has frequently participated in international exercises like **RIMPAC** and **MALABAR**, showcasing the **Indian Navy's** blue-water capabilities across the **Indian** and **Pacific Oceans**.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which of the following new mottos was adopted by the Lokpal of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Empower Citizens, Expose Corruption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lokpal of India**, the country’s apex anti-corruption body, officially adopted its new motto, "**Empower Citizens, Expose Corruption**," in the year **2025**.
 
• The adoption of this new motto signifies a strategic shift towards encouraging **proactive public participation** in the fight against graft and administrative malpractice.
 
• This change was aimed at making the institution more **accessible and citizen-centric**, moving away from purely reactive legal frameworks to a more inclusive social movement against corruption.
 
• The previous motto of the Lokpal was "**Ma Gridhah Kasyasvidhanam**," which translates to "Do not be greedy for anyone’s wealth," derived from the **Isha Upanishad**. 
 
• The new branding, including the motto, was selected to resonate with the **youth of India** and the digital-age requirements of **transparency and accountability**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Empower Citizens, Expose Corruption.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:**
 
 
• The institution of Lokpal was established under the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act**, which was passed by Parliament in **December 2013** and received Presidential assent on **January 1, 2014**.
 
• The act provides for the establishment of a **Lokpal for the Union** and **Lokayukta for the States** to inquire into allegations of corruption against certain public functionaries.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal consists of a **Chairperson** and a maximum of **eight members**, out of which **50%** must be **Judicial Members**.
 
• At least **50%** of the members must come from **SC, ST, OBC, minorities, and women** categories to ensure diverse representation.
 
• The **Selection Committee** for the Lokpal is headed by the **Prime Minister** and includes the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of the Opposition, the **Chief Justice of India**, and an eminent jurist.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction and Powers:**
 
 
• The jurisdiction of the Lokpal includes the **Prime Minister**, Ministers in the Union government, **Members of Parliament**, and officials of **Groups A, B, C, and D** under the Central Government.
 
• It has the power to supervise and give directions to the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** regarding cases referred to them by the Lokpal.
 
• The Lokpal has the powers of a **Civil Court** and can order the **attachment of property** acquired through corrupt means, even while the inquiry is ongoing.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The term "Lokpal" was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963**.
 
• The first **Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC)**, headed by **Morarji Desai** in **1966**, recommended the setting up of two independent authorities (Lokpal and Lokayukta) to redress citizens' grievances.
 
• The **first Lokpal Chairperson** of India, Justice **Pinaki Chandra Ghose**, was appointed in **March 2019**.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the Arjuna Award in 2025 for their performance in para-athletics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deepthi Jeevanji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deepthi Jeevanji** is a prominent **Indian Para-athlete** who was honored with the **Arjuna Award** in **January 2025** for her stellar achievements in **para-athletics**.
 
• She specializes in the **400m sprint** and competes in the **T20 category**, which is designated for athletes with **intellectual impairments**.
 
• One of her most significant career milestones was winning the **Bronze Medal** at the **Paris Paralympics 2024**, where she finished the **women's 400m T20** final with a timing of **55.82 seconds**.
 
• In **May 2024**, she created history by setting a new **World Record** in the **women's 400m T20** event at the **World Para Athletics Championships** held in **Kobe, Japan**, clocking **55.07 seconds**.
 
• Hailing from **Kalledu village** in the **Warangal district** of **Telangana**, her recognition with the **Arjuna Award** highlights the increasing prominence of para-sports in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arjuna Award:**
 
 
• Established in **1961**, the **Arjuna Award** is **India's second-highest sporting honor**, conferred by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• It is awarded to sportspersons for **consistent outstanding performance** over a period of **four years**, along with qualities of leadership, sportsmanship, and discipline.
 
• The award includes a **bronze statuette of Arjuna**, a certificate, and a cash prize of **Rs. 15 lakh**.
 
 
 
• **Manu Bhaker (Shooting):**
 
 
• **Manu Bhaker** is an elite **Indian Shooter** who made history at the **Paris Olympics 2024** by winning **two Bronze Medals** in a single Olympic edition.
 
• She won her medals in the **Women's 10m Air Pistol** and the **Mixed Team 10m Air Pistol** events, becoming a leading figure in Indian **shooting**.
 
 
 
• **Harmanpreet Singh (Hockey):**
 
 
• Often referred to as the **"Sarpanch,"** **Harmanpreet Singh** is the captain of the **Indian Men’s National Hockey Team**.
 
• Under his leadership, the team secured a **Bronze Medal** at the **Paris Olympics 2024**, following their success at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Gukesh D (Chess):**
 
 
• **Gukesh Dommaraju**, known as **Gukesh D**, is a **Chess Grandmaster** who became the youngest-ever winner of the **FIDE Candidates Tournament** in **2024**.
 
• His performance earned him the right to challenge for the **World Chess Championship**, and he was a key member of the Indian team that won **Gold** at the **45th Chess Olympiad** in **Budapest**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **National Sports Awards 2024** (conferred in **2025**) saw a significant representation of athletes who excelled in the **Paris Olympic** and **Paralympic Games**.
 
• **India** achieved its best-ever medal haul at the **Paris Paralympics 2024**, winning a total of **29 medals**, including **7 Gold**, **9 Silver**, and **13 Bronze**.
 
• The **T20 classification** in **Para-athletics** is specifically for athletes with an **IQ below 75**, who have significant limitations in adaptive behavior, which manifests before the **age of 18**.
 
• The recognition of para-athletes like **Deepthi Jeevanji** serves as a major boost for **inclusive sports** policies under the **Khelo India** initiative and the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**.

questions.question: With which government did the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change sign a Memorandum of Cooperation on Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change, in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, Government of India, signed a **Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC)** with the Government of **Japan** in **August 2025** to implement the **Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM)**.
 
• This partnership is established under **Article 6.2** of the **Paris Agreement**, which encourages international cooperation through market-based mechanisms to achieve **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**.
 
• The primary objective of the **JCM** is to facilitate the diffusion of advanced **low-carbon technologies** and infrastructure from **Japan** to **India**, promoting sustainable development and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions.
 
• As part of the agreement, a **Joint Committee** consisting of representatives from both governments will be established to oversee the implementation, project registration, and issuance of **carbon credits**.
 
• The mechanism ensures that emission reductions or removals are verified and can be used by both **India** and **Japan** to meet their respective climate targets under the **Paris Agreement**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Japan.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM):**
 
 
• It is a **bilateral system** initiated by **Japan** to incentivize the transfer of **decarbonizing technologies** to partner countries.
 
• The **JCM** helps **Japan** achieve its target of **Net Zero by 2050** while supporting the transition of developing nations toward **green energy**.
 
• Credits generated through **JCM** projects are allocated to the participating parties, ensuring that there is no **double counting** of emission reductions.
 
 
 
• **Article 6 of the Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• **Article 6.2**: Focuses on **bilateral or multilateral cooperation** through **Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs)**.
 
• **Article 6.4**: Establishes a global carbon market overseen by a **United Nations** body, replacing the **Clean Development Mechanism (CDM)** of the **Kyoto Protocol**.
 
• **Article 6.8**: Promotes non-market-based approaches, such as **climate finance** and technology transfer, without the exchange of credits.
 
 
 
• **India's Climate Commitments:**
 
 
• India has committed to achieving **Net Zero emissions by 2070**, as announced during **COP26** in **Glasgow**.
 
• India's updated **NDCs** include reducing the **emission intensity** of its **GDP by 45%** by **2030** compared to **2005** levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Japan's Global Partnerships:** Apart from **India**, **Japan** has signed **JCM** agreements with more than **25 partner countries**, including **Vietnam**, **Thailand**, **Indonesia**, and **Saudi Arabia**.
 
• **Technological Scope:** The **MoC** covers various sectors such as **renewable energy** (solar, wind), **energy efficiency** in industries, **waste-to-energy** projects, and **green hydrogen** production.
 
• **MoEFCC Role:** The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** serves as the nodal ministry in **India** for coordinating international climate negotiations and domestic climate policy implementation.
</ul

questions.question: In which city were the Khelo India Para Games 2025, a significant event under the Khelo India scheme, held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khelo India Para Games 2025** is a major initiative under the **Khelo India** program, held in the capital city of **New Delhi**.
 
• This event is specifically designed to provide a national-level platform for **para-athletes** (athletes with disabilities) to showcase their skills and talent.
 
• The games are organized by the **Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** and were established to fill the gap in competitive opportunities for the **Divyang** sporting community.
 
• **New Delhi** serves as the primary host due to its accessible infrastructure and world-class sporting facilities like the **Indira Gandhi Stadium**, **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium**, and **Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range**.
 
• The goal of the 2025 edition remains consistent with the program's vision: to foster **inclusivity**, promote sports as a tool for empowerment, and identify potential medalists for international events like the **Paralympics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Programme:**
 
 
• Launched in **2018**, the **Khelo India** (Play India) scheme was introduced to revive the sports culture at the grass-root level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the country.
 
• It encompasses several verticals including the **Khelo India Youth Games**, **Khelo India University Games**, **Khelo India Winter Games**, and the newly added **Para Games**.
 
 
 
• **History of Para Games:**
 
 
• The inaugural edition of the **Khelo India Para Games** was held in **December 2023** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The mascot for the first games was **'Ujjwala'**, a sparrow, which represents the pride, determination, and spirit of the athletes.
 
 
 
• **Scholarships and Support:**
 
 
• Under the scheme, talented players identified in priority sports disciplines at various levels are provided annual financial assistance of **Rs. 5 lakh** per annum for **8 years**.
 
• This long-term support is crucial for athletes coming from economically weaker backgrounds to sustain their training and nutrition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sports Disciplines:** The event covers numerous disciplines, including **Para Athletics**, **Para Archery**, **Para Football**, **Para Badminton**, **Para Table Tennis**, **Para Shooting**, and **Para Powerlifting**.
 
• **Participation:** Athletes from over **30 States and Union Territories** typically participate, making it a pan-India movement for the differently-abled.
 
• **Digital Integration:** The government utilizes the **Khelo India Mobile App** and a dedicated portal to manage registrations, schedules, and live updates, ensuring transparency and ease of access for participants.
 
• **Infrastructure Accessibility:** A significant focus of holding the games in **New Delhi** is to demonstrate and improve **"Accessible India" (Sugamya Bharat)** standards across major stadium complexes.
</ul

questions.question: The 10th Governing Council Meeting of NITI Aayog on 24 May 2025 was held in which city of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **10th Governing Council Meeting** of the **NITI Aayog** was held on **24 May 2025**.
 
• The meeting took place in **New Delhi**, which serves as the traditional venue for the **Governing Council** deliberations due to its status as the **National Capital**.
 
• The session was chaired by the **Prime Minister of India**, who is the **Ex-officio Chairperson** of **NITI Aayog**.
 
• The core agenda of this high-level meeting centered around the roadmap for **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**, focusing on making **India** a **developed nation** by the **100th year** of its **Independence**.
 
• It served as a platform to discuss **inter-sectoral** and **inter-departmental** issues to accelerate the implementation of various **National Development Priorities**. ***Hence, the correct answer is New Delhi.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)**:
 
 
• It was established on **1 January 2015**, replacing the erstwhile **Planning Commission** which followed a top-down model.
 
• It operates as the **premier policy think-tank** of the **Government of India**, providing both directional and policy inputs.
 
• The institution is built on the pillars of **Cooperative Federalism**, ensuring that **States** are active partners in the **national development** process.
 
 
 
• **Composition of the Governing Council**:
 
 
• The council comprises the **Prime Minister** of India, **Chief Ministers** of all the **States**, and **Chief Ministers** of **Union Territories** with Legislatures (like **Delhi** and **Puducherry**).
 
• It also includes the **Lieutenant Governors** of other **Union Territories** and **Ex-officio Members**, along with **Special Invitees**.
 
• The **Governing Council** is the most significant body of **NITI Aayog**, tasked with evolving a shared vision of **national priorities**.
 
 
 
• **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**:
 
 
• This is a strategic government initiative to transform **India** into a **developed economy** by **2047**.
 
• Key focus areas include **structural reforms**, **digital infrastructure**, **sustainable energy**, and **inclusive growth**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Organizational Structure**:
 
 
• **Vice-Chairperson**: Appointed by the **Prime Minister** and enjoys the rank of a **Cabinet Minister**.
 
• **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**: Appointed by the **Prime Minister** for a fixed tenure, holding the rank of **Secretary** to the **Government of India**.
 
• **Hubs**: **NITI Aayog** houses two main hubs: the **Team India Hub** (facilitating state participation) and the **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** (building think-tank capabilities).
 
 
 
• **Previous Meetings**:
 
 
• The **9th Governing Council meeting** was held in **July 2024**, which also focused on themes of **Cooperative Federalism** and **economic governance**.
 
• These meetings are essential for aligning **State-level** policies with **National** goals to ensure **synchronized development** across the **country**.
 
 
</ul

• In **August 2025**, the **Indian Army** inaugurated a specialized research cell named **Agnishodh** at the **Indian Institute of Technology Madras** (**IIT Madras**) in **Chennai**.
 
• The primary objective of **Agnishodh** is to bridge the gap between military operational requirements and academic research by fostering a collaborative environment for **defense innovation**.
 
• The cell focuses on developing **niche technologies** and **indigenous solutions** to enhance the combat capabilities and operational efficiency of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• This initiative is a strategic step towards achieving self-reliance in defense technology, aligning with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** vision of the **Government of India**.
 
• By establishing this cell at **IIT Madras**, the **Indian Army** aims to leverage the institute's cutting-edge infrastructure and intellectual capital to solve complex technical challenges faced on the battlefield.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IIT Madras and Defense Research:** 
 
 
• **IIT Madras** has a long-standing history of partnering with the **Ministry of Defence** and **DRDO** (**Defence Research and Development Organisation**) for various high-tech projects.
 
• The institute has been a pioneer in **deep-tech startups** through its **Incubation Cell**, many of which provide solutions for **security** and **surveillance**.
 
 
 
• **Modernization of the Indian Army:** 
 
 
• The **Indian Army** is increasingly focusing on **modernization** through the **Army Technology Board (ATB)** to integrate **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Machine Learning**, and **Robotics** into its hardware.
 
• The establishment of **Agnishodh** reflects the shift toward **indigenous manufacturing** under the **Make in India** initiative in the defense sector.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas of Research:** 
 
 
• The research at such cells typically encompasses **Cybersecurity**, **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)**, **Quantum Communication**, and **Advanced Material Science** for ballistic protection.
 
• These advancements are crucial for maintaining a technological edge in **hybrid warfare** and **border management**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Impact:** The **Agnishodh** cell facilitates direct interaction between **soldiers** and **scientists**, ensuring that the technology developed is practical and suited for harsh terrains like **Ladakh** or the **Thar Desert**.
 
• **Innovation Ecosystem:** This model encourages **Technology Transfer (ToT)** from academia to **Defense Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)** and private industry partners for mass production.
 
• **Year of Initiative:** The launch in **2025** marks a significant milestone in the **Indian Army's** timeline of academic institutional partnerships, following similar models at **IIT Delhi** and **IIT Bombay**.
 
• **National Security:** By reducing dependence on **foreign OEMs (Original Equipment Manufacturers)**, **Agnishodh** contributes to the long-term **strategic autonomy** of **India**.

questions.question: Which of the following has been declared a Tiger Reserve in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav Tiger Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Madhav Tiger Reserve**, located in the **Shivpuri** district of **Madhya Pradesh**, has been officially notified as a tiger reserve in **January 2025**.
 
• It has become the **56th Tiger Reserve** in India and the **8th** such reserve in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The notification follows the successful reintroduction of tigers into the park which began in **March 2023**, aimed at restoring the predator population in the **Vindhyan landscape**.
 
• The **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** gave its final nod for the declaration to ensure better administrative control and financial support for tiger protection.
 
• Historically, the area served as the hunting grounds for the **Scindia dynasty** of Gwalior and the **Mughal emperors**, highlighting its long-standing ecological significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched on **April 1, 1973**, from **Jim Corbett National Park**, it is a centrally sponsored scheme of the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
 
• It aims to ensure a viable population of Bengal tigers in their natural habitats and protect them from extinction.
 
 
 
• **Tiger State of India:**
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** holds the title of **"Tiger State"** as it hosts the highest number of tigers in India as per the **2022 Census**.
 
• Other prominent reserves in the state include **Kanha**, **Bandhavgarh**, **Panna**, **Pench**, **Satpura**, **Sanjay-Dubri**, and **Veerangana Durgavati**.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):**
 
 
• Established in **December 2005**, it is a **statutory body** under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• The **Minister in charge** of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is the **Chairperson** of the NTCA.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Statistics:**
 
 
• India is home to approximately **75%** of the world's wild tiger population.
 
• The **Status of Tigers in India 2022** report estimated the minimum population at **3,167** tigers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dholpur – Karauli Tiger Reserve:** Located in **Rajasthan**, it was declared as the **55th** Tiger Reserve of India in **2023**.
 
• **Ranipur Tiger Reserve:** Situated in the **Chitrakoot** district of **Uttar Pradesh**, it was notified as the **53rd** reserve in **2022**.
 
• **Parambikulam Tiger Reserve:** Located in the **Palakkad** district of **Kerala**, it was declared a tiger reserve in **2009-2010**.
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The **Madhav Tiger Reserve** acts as a crucial link between the **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in Rajasthan and the **Panna Tiger Reserve** in Madhya Pradesh, creating a vital **wildlife corridor**.
 
• **Flora and Fauna:** The park is characterized by **Northern Tropical Dry Deciduous** mixed forests and **Thorn forests**, and it is home to the **Sakhya Sagar** lake, which is a designated **Ramsar Site**.

questions.question: On which date was World Malaria Day 2025 observed with the theme Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April 25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Malaria Day** is an international observance commemorated every year on **April 25** to recognize global efforts to control malaria.
 
• The theme for **World Malaria Day 2025** is "**Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite**." This theme calls for a renewed commitment to funding, innovative strategies, and a reinvigorated spirit to eliminate the disease.
 
• The day was established by the **World Health Assembly** at its **60th session** in **May 2007**. It was designed to provide education and understanding of malaria and spread information on year-long intensified implementation of national malaria-control strategies.
 
• Before **World Malaria Day**, **Africa Malaria Day** was observed on the same date, starting in **2001**, following the historic **Abuja Declaration** by **44** malaria-endemic countries.
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** uses this platform to highlight the need for continued investment and sustained political commitment for malaria prevention and control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disease Profile**: **Malaria** is a life-threatening disease caused by **Plasmodium parasites** that are transmitted to people through the bites of infected female **Anopheles mosquitoes**. Among the five parasite species that cause malaria in humans, **P. falciparum** and **P. vivax** pose the greatest threat.
 
• **Prevention and Treatment**: Key interventions include the use of **Long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs)**, **Indoor residual spraying (IRS)**, and **Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT)** for treatment.
 
• **Vaccine Development**: A major milestone was reached with the recommendation of the **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** vaccine in **October 2021** and the **R21/Matrix-M** vaccine in **2023** for children living in regions with moderate to high malaria transmission.
 
• **Global Burden**: According to the **World Malaria Report**, the **WHO African Region** carries a disproportionately high share of the global malaria burden, accounting for approximately **94%** of cases and **95%** of deaths globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SDG Target**: The **United Nations** Sustainable Development Goal **(SDG) 3.3** aims to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, **malaria**, and neglected tropical diseases by the **year 2030**.
 
• **Elimination Certification**: The **WHO** grants a "**Malaria-Free Certification**" to countries that have demonstrated, beyond a reasonable doubt, that the chain of indigenous transmission has been interrupted nationwide for at least the consecutive **last 3 years**.
 
• **Recent Successes**: In **2023**, **Azerbaijan** and **Tajikistan** were certified malaria-free, followed by **Cabo Verde** in early **2024**, showcasing that elimination is achievable with persistent effort.
 
• **Global Technical Strategy**: The **WHO Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030** aims to reduce malaria case incidence and mortality rates by at least **90%** by **2030** compared to **2015** levels.

questions.question: In 2025, which ministry of the Government of India organised Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan for ranking air quality in Indian cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** is an initiative by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to rank cities on the basis of air quality and the implementation of activities approved under the city action plan.
 
• The primary objective of the survey is to rank **131 non-attainment cities** in the country that have consistently failed to meet the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for **five consecutive years**.
 
• For the year **2025**, the ministry continues to use this ranking system to foster a spirit of healthy competition among cities and encourage them to take proactive measures to reduce **air pollution**.
 
• The ranking is based on the **self-assessment** of cities on the **PRANA** (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities) portal, where cities report their progress on **eight thematic areas**.
 
• These thematic areas include **biomass and municipal solid waste burning**, **road dust**, **dust from construction and demolition waste**, **vehicular emissions**, **industrial emissions**, **public awareness**, and **improvements in PM10 concentrations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2019**, the **NCAP** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across the country.
 
• The programme initially aimed for a **20% to 30% reduction** in **PM2.5 and PM10** concentrations by **2024**, keeping **2017** as the base year for comparison.
 
• The goal was later updated to achieve a **40% reduction** in particulate matter concentrations by the year **2026**.
 
 
 
• **City Categories:**
 
 
• Cities are classified into three categories for the survey based on their population as per the **2011 Census**.
 
• **Category 1:** Cities with a population of **more than 10 Lakh** (over 47 cities).
 
• **Category 2:** Cities with a population between **3 Lakh to 10 Lakh** (44 cities).
 
• **Category 3:** Cities with a population **less than 3 Lakh** (40 cities).
 
 
 
• **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies:**
 
 
• The awards for the best-performing cities under the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** are typically presented on **September 7th**, which is observed globally as the **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies**.
 
• This day was designated by the **United Nations General Assembly** in **2019** to emphasize the need for further efforts to improve air quality to protect human health.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of CPCB:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** plays a technical role in overseeing the air quality monitoring data and assisting the **Ministry of Environment** in the verification of city reports.
 
• **PRANA Portal:** The **PRANA** portal serves as a digital platform for monitoring the implementation of **NCAP**. It provides real-time information on the air quality status of **non-attainment cities** and tracks the progress of various mitigation activities.
 
• **Difference from AQI:** While the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** provides a real-time daily measurement of air health, the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** is a comprehensive annual ranking based on **policy implementation** and **long-term improvements** in air quality parameters.
 
• **Incentives:** The top-performing cities in each category receive **cash awards** and trophies to support further environmental conservation initiatives, funded by the **Government of India**.
</ul

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey 2024–25, which scheme electrified over 18,000 villages in rural India?

options.text: Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All (UJALA)
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)** is a flagship scheme of the **Ministry of Power** designed to provide continuous power supply to rural India.
 
• As noted in the **Economic Survey 2024–25**, the scheme was instrumental in achieving the massive milestone of electrifying **18,374 un-electrified villages** across the country.
 
• The scheme was launched on **July 25, 2015**, by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in **Patna, Bihar**, with the aim of revolutionizing the rural power distribution system.
 
• It focused on several key objectives: the **separation of agriculture and non-agriculture feeders**, strengthening of **sub-transmission and distribution networks**, and the **electrification of villages**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY).***
 
• The scheme subsumed the previous **Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY)** while keeping the rural electrification targets as a primary component.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UJALA (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2015**, it is considered the world's largest **LED bulb** distribution program.
 
• It aims to promote energy efficiency by providing high-quality **LEDs** to domestic consumers at affordable prices, significantly reducing **electricity bills** and **carbon emissions**.
 
 
 
• **UDAY (Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana):**
 
 
• Launched in **November 2015**, this scheme targets the **financial turnaround** and revival of Power Distribution Companies (**DISCOMs**).
 
• It focuses on four areas: improving operational efficiency of DISCOMs, reduction of **cost of power**, reduction in **interest burden**, and enforcing **financial discipline**.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Nayi Roshni Yojana (PMNRY):**
 
 
• This is primarily a **Leadership Development Program** for **Minority Women** launched by the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**.
 
• It aims to empower and instill confidence among minority women by providing knowledge, tools, and techniques for interacting with **Government systems** and **Banks**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Universal Village Electrification:** The goal of 100% village electrification was declared complete on **April 28, 2018**, when **Leisang** village in the **Senapati** district of **Manipur** was connected to the **national grid**.
 
• **Shift to Household Electrification:** Following the success of **DDUGJY** in reaching every village, the government launched the **SAUBHAGYA** (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) in **October 2017** to ensure **last-mile connectivity** to all un-electrified households.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** The **Economic Survey 2024–25** highlights that the enhancement of the **power sector infrastructure** has been a critical driver for **GDP growth** and improved **Ease of Living** in rural areas.
 
• **Technical Components:** Under **DDUGJY**, the **Rural Electrification Corporation (REC)** acted as the **Nodal Agency** for the operationalization and monitoring of the projects.
